sections.title: Market Pulse: Wall Street Rebounds on Earnings and Easing Rate Hike Concerns

items.headline: U.S. equities closed higher on Wednesday, snapping a three-day losing streak, as strong earnings reports bolstered investor sentiment despite ongoing geopolitical tensions and fluctuating bond yields.
items.summary: Major indices saw gains, driven by positive corporate results and comments from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller suggesting a potential hold on interest rates, contingent on upcoming inflation data. Oil prices continued to climb due to escalating U.S.-Iran conflict, yet Treasury yields showed signs of easing by Thursday morning.

items.headline: Dell Technologies surged on strong quarterly results.
items.summary: Dell Technologies saw its stock jump 15.8% after reporting robust quarterly revenues of $286.25 million, which surpassed consensus estimates by 4.74% and were up 21.3% year-over-year.

items.headline: Snowflake experienced a significant pre-market rally due to strong earnings.
items.summary: Snowflake Inc. shares surged over 20% in Thursday's pre-market trading, following strong after-hours earnings and increased full-year product revenue guidance, signaling extended enterprise AI demand.

items.headline: Nvidia advanced on AI acquisition news.
items.summary: Nvidia gained 3.2% at Wednesday's close, further boosted by the announcement of its intention to acquire AI platform Hugging Face for $13 billion.

items.headline: G-III Apparel Group shares plunged after missing revenue estimates.
items.summary: G-III Apparel Group Ltd. plummeted 11.5% after its second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $554.09 million fell short of Zacks Consensus Estimates.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks fell due to disappointing guidance.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Inc. saw its stock fall 9.3% after reporting fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 Subscription and Support revenues and adjusted gross profits below consensus expectations.

items.headline: SK Hynix shares dropped in Thursday's pre-market.
items.summary: The memory sector underperformed in Thursday's pre-market, with SK Hynix shares falling over 3% amid news of a potential Micron Taiwan union strike and increasing market share by China's CXMT.

items.headline: Fed Governor Waller Signals Potential Rate Hold Based on Upcoming Inflation Data
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller indicated on Thursday that the August inflation report, due September 11, would be crucial in determining his stance on interest rates. He is inclined to support holding rates steady if disinflation continues, but remains open to a hike if inflation accelerates.

items.headline: U.S. Trade Deficit Widens in July 2026
items.summary: The U.S. goods and services deficit expanded to $88.6 billion in July, an increase of $17.4 billion from June's revised figure. Exports declined by 2.1%, while imports rose by 2.8%.

items.headline: Nonfarm Business Labor Productivity Increased in Q2 2026
items.summary: Revised data for the second quarter of 2026 showed nonfarm business sector labor productivity increasing by 1.4%, with output up 1.7% and hours worked increasing 0.3%. Unit labor costs rose by 1.2%.

items.headline: Energy Leads, Tech and Discretionary Lagged on Wednesday
items.summary: On Wednesday, the Energy Select Sector SPDR ($XLE) was a leading sector, rising 1.3%. In contrast, sectors like Consumer Discretionary ($XLY), Information Technology ($XLK), Materials ($XLB), and Industrials ($XLI) all saw declines. However, the AI boom continues to drive individual tech stock performances.

items.headline: Oil Prices Remain Elevated Amid U.S.-Iran Conflict Escalation
items.summary: Crude oil prices continued to climb due to intensifying U.S.-Iran tensions. Brent crude reached an intraday high of $97.62 per barrel on Thursday, indicating persistent geopolitical risk to inflation.
